speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are experiencing knee pain after recently increasing your physical activity. To help me narrow down the cause, can you describe exactly where the pain is located and what specific movements make it worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The recent volleyball pivoting suggests a ligament or meniscus injury, but to confirm the specific structure involved, does the knee pop or lock when you try to bend it, and is there significant swelling? Also, have you been able to bear any weight on the leg since the pain started?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Osgood-Schlatter Disease

The specific location of your pain over the tibial tubercle, combined with your age and recent increase in physical activity, strongly points to Osgover-Schlatter disease. Has the area been tender to touch, and have you noticed any visible bump or swelling directly over that spot?
